title: The 10 Hottest Female Rappers of 2026 Right Now: Staff Picks
summary: For the third straight year, Billboard's editorial staff highlights the hottest female MCs to this point in 2026.
contentText:
For the third annual edition of Billboard’s Hottest Female Rappers List, the competition has reached new heights. The field is deeper, the bars are sharper, and the music continues to push the genre forward.

Last year, Cardi B emerged as the last woman standing following a remarkable comeback campaign. After a seven-year hiatus, the Bronx superstar reclaimed her spot atop the conversation, reminding hip-hop why she’s one of its defining forces with her Billboard 200 No. 1 album, Am I the Drama?

But Cardi’s resurgence was only part of the story. A wave of breakout stars stormed onto the scene and immediately shifted the landscape. Bunna B, Pluto and YK Niece announced themselves with explosive club anthems, while South Carolina native Trim burst into the conversation with her glossy delivery and animated flow. Meanwhile, Samara Cyn continued her ascent as one of rap’s most intriguing new voices, blending genres with a fearless creativity that has her knocking on the door of stardom.

One artist who embodied resilience this year was Yung Miami. After the City Girls dissolved and JT scored her own breakthrough with the Billboard Hot 100 hit “OKAY,” many wondered whether Miami could carve out a successful solo path. She answered emphatically, silencing skeptics with the top 20 hit “Spend Dat” while delivering one of the strongest song-of-the-summer contenders in the process.

As in previous years, Billboard’s editorial staff ranked this year’s Hottest Female Rappers using a combination of record quality, chart performance, cultural impact, business ventures, brand partnerships and touring success.

Read on to see who made Billboard’s year-end Hottest Female Rappers list and check back later this December to find out who ultimately claims the crown.
